page.layout: One column of verse, indented stanzas, running head above the text. No page number, catchword or signature is printed.

main_text.p: Et iam nutanti sub pondere sponte fatiscat, Seque sui tandem penitus, penitúsque ruina Obruat, & sceleris scelus hauriat alta vorago.

Vos igitur quos tanta tenet fiducia vitæ Et scelerum, rebus nunc indulgetæ caducis, Ite: sed ista olim constabunt gaudia magno. Mox aderit tempus, quum iam quas mente secatis Spes interdictas, & inania vota per auras Discerpent venti, fastúmque animósque feroces Molliet una dies, tandémque dolere docebit.

Ergo age Roma tuos age; fac pia Roma Cynædos Securos scelerum, satia te sanguine iusto Dum licet, & nullum tibi fac iam crimen inausum. Exulta fidens quantumlibet, omnia tenta Infamis Babylon: terræ commune lupanar Roma (Lupæ nam cur author tuus vbera frustra Suxisset?) meritam quæ te obuoluere tenebræ? O si te quis iam manet exitus ante videres! Nam tibi mox gemitum & lachrymas miserósque vlulatus, Vltrices furias, & ineluctabile fatum Attulerit iam summa dies, tibi sera gementi Ride age terrarúmque nefas crimenque Sodome Impia: quod si nunc cæli te languida claudo Securam vindicta gradu sequitúrue premitue Ingenti, nec adhuc ferri trabe frangit auaros Pontifices, miserúmque istum infamémque Dialem Quem nimium heu nimium funesta Lutetia novit, Hoc mage terribilem spera scelerata ruinam. Sera pedes lanæ instar habet vindicta, sed acres Ingeminans ictus, & ferrea brachia quassans Per populos; pede profubigit calcátque tiaras Pontificum Regúmque, magistratusque superbos, Aeratis quondam audaces qui frontibus audent Insultare Deo & lentum irridere furorem

page.notes: Lines 1-3 and the verse continuation at the top are a fragment carried over from the previous page. The mark after "Sod" in "Sodome" is a small sign I could not read with certainty; it is copied as printed. Italic setting is judged from the scan and may be incomplete. Some words near the lines "Securam vindicta" and "Pontifices" are small or blurred and may contain printing errors left as printed (e.g. "premitue", "nouit", "Dialem"). The "&" signs are the italic et-sign as printed.
